content.user_title: Improve Go Code With Best Practices
content.value_statement: Go projects can drift into weak types, unclear interfaces, and inconsistent error handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward idiomatic Go patterns.
actual_capabilities: Recommends custom domain types for identifiers and primitives.
Describes focused interfaces that model required behavior.
Shows enum-style constants with explicit default error handling.
Demonstrates functional options for flexible constructors.
Explains error wrapping with Go error chain preservation.
Promotes structured logging with log/slog key-value pairs.
limitations: Provides guidance only and does not execute Go tooling.
Covers selected language idioms, not complete architecture review.
Examples may need imports, tests, and project-specific adaptation.
Does not include deep security hardening guidance for Go services.

use_cases.title: Review Go Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check whether new code uses strong types, focused interfaces, and clear error handling.

use_cases.title: Design Cleaner APIs
use_cases.description: Shape constructors, repositories, and domain types before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Coach Go Beginners
use_cases.description: Teach practical idioms through small examples that explain why each pattern matters.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Go Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go file for type safety, interface design, error wrapping, and structured logging. Give concise recommendations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one Go file

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Domain Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest domain-specific Go types for identifiers and status values in this package. Explain each proposed type in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Construction Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these constructors and configuration options. Recommend where functional options would make the API clearer.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Service Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Go service boundary for focused interfaces, context usage, error chains, and structured logging. Prioritize issues by impact.

output_examples.input: Review a Go package that passes string IDs between repository methods.
output: Use a dedicated user identifier type to prevent mixing it with other identifiers.
Keep repository interfaces small and define them near the consumer.
Wrap returned errors with operation context so callers can inspect the chain.

output_examples.input: Improve a server constructor with many optional settings.
output: Replace long parameter lists with named options for optional settings.
Keep defaults inside the constructor so callers only specify changes.
Document each option by the behavior it changes.

output_examples.input: Check logging in a widget creation function.
output: Use structured key-value fields instead of formatted text.
Attach stable component metadata to the logger.
Avoid logging secrets or raw request payloads.

best_practices: Use domain-specific types when plain primitives can be confused.
Accept small interfaces that describe caller needs.
Wrap errors with operation context and preserve the original cause.
anti_patterns: Passing raw strings for every identifier in domain code.
Creating broad interfaces before a real consumer needs them.
Replacing error context with plain text that hides the original cause.

faq.question: Does this skill write Go code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for an AI assistant. The assistant may edit files only when the user asks it to.

faq.question: Which Go topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers type safety, interfaces, enum-style constants, functional options, error wrapping, and structured logging.

faq.question: Can it run gofmt or tests?
faq.answer: No. The skill text does not define commands or scripts for running Go tools.

faq.question: Is it useful for new Go developers?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples focus on common idioms and explain patterns through small code samples.

faq.question: Does it replace a full code review?
faq.answer: No. It is a focused checklist for selected Go practices, not a complete review process.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
